course: an illustrated online course on textiles and their history for adults with no textile background
intro: Part I (lessons 1 to 5) teaches how cloth is made: fibre, yarn, woven and knitted structure, and colour. Part II runs in time order from Roman purple to cotton today, on trade, empire, slavery, industry and work. Each lesson opens on a documented scene, object or account with real people, places and dates. Plain, direct technical prose in the manner of Virginia Postrel's The Fabric of Civilization: precise terms (warp, weft, drafting, mordant), units kept, no aphorisms, no literary flourishes, no rhetorical questions, no inanimate agency. Slavery, removal and factory deaths are stated plainly with numbers, without melodrama. Legends are told as legends, and contested numbers are not stated as fact. Do not change the words inside quotation marks.
